target.title: fix(agents): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in find tool
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `find` tool spawns `fd`/`find` and reads stdout/stderr through a `readline` interface. If either stream emits an error before or during line processing, the error is not handled, which can crash the agent process with an unhandled exception.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the fix already applied to `bash` (#101005) and `grep` (#101014): attach explicit error handlers to both the readline interface and the raw stdout/stderr streams so transient stream errors are logged and the tool result reflects the failure instead of propagating an unhandled exception.

## User Impact

Agent runs using the `find` tool are more resilient to OS-level stream failures (e.g., pipe errors, resource limits).

## Evidence

- Added regression tests in `src/agents/sessions/tools/find.fd.test.ts` covering both stdout and stderr stream errors.
- Added a real behavior proof script at `scripts/proof/find-tool-stream-errors.mts` that spawns the tool and forces a stream error, verifying the process does not crash.
- Local run:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.fd.test.ts` passed
  - `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts src/agents/sessions/tools/find.fd.test.ts` passed
